preventive_tips: Plant rust-resistant sugarcane varieties (e.g. Co 0238, Co 86032).
Ensure optimal inter-row spacing to promote sunlight penetration and lower humidity.
153.treatment: Sugarcane Rust detected. Spray Propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L) or Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5g/L) across the canopy.

symptoms: Broad, vibrant green leaves with sturdy white midribs and clean leaf cuticles.
No red rot discoloration, rust pustules, yellowing, or viral enations.
Vigorous, thick stalk internodes with intact root eyes and healthy shoot buds.
organic_remedies: Apply well-rotted press mud cake or vermicompost in furrows.
Inoculate soil with Gluconacetobacter diazotrophicus nitrogen-fixing bio-fertilizer.
chemical_remedies: Apply recommended NPK schedule (150:60:60 kg/ha in split doses).
Apply Ferrous Sulfate (5g/L) if iron chlorosis appears in alkaline soils.
preventive_tips: Earthing up at 90-120 days to support stalks against lodging.
Maintain trash mulching in furrows to conserve soil moisture and suppress weeds.
154.treatment: Sugarcane crop is completely healthy. Continue split nitrogen-potash fertilization, trash mulching, and earthing up.

symptoms: Contrasting chlorotic yellow-green and dark green mottled patches or stripes on leaf lamina.
Discoloration most prominent on young expanding leaves near the spindle whorl.
Stunting of infected stalks, reduced tillering, and shortened internodes.
organic_remedies: Eradicate aphid vectors using yellow sticky traps and cold-pressed Neem oil (3ml/L).
Hot water treatment of planting setts at 52°C for 30 minutes.
chemical_remedies: Control aphid vectors using Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.5ml/L) or Acetamiprid 20 SP (0.5g/L).
Foliar spray of micronutrient complex with Zinc and Iron to mitigate chlorotic stress.
preventive_tips: Plant certified virus-free setts from registered tissue culture nurseries.
Rogue out and destroy infected stools immediately upon symptom appearance.
155.treatment: Sugarcane Mosaic Virus detected. Control aphid vectors with Imidacloprid (0.5ml/L) and remove infected stools.
